articles.headline: Now Ready! Masonry and Christianity! Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller's Great Sermon (advertisement)
articles.summary: NOW READY! Masonry and Christianity! Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller's Great Sermon, as delivered before the higher orders of [Masonry], at the Central Presbyterian church. Sold at 25 cents per copy, and may be had of the Committee or of the author, [No. illegible] Quince Street. Every Mason and every opposer of Masonry should have a copy. May 25-4 on ha.(?)
people: author of the sermon (Rev.); printed 'Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller's'; middle name partly broken in the type

articles.headline: Afflicted with Envy-Mania (editorial on the Zion's Standard and the retiring editor)
articles.summary: The many kind and complimentary words spoken by several of our exchanges, in reference to the retiring editor, Rev. James Lynch, affords pleasure to all connected with our office, as we know the worth of the man we lose. One single exchange paper, one only, has spoken unkindly, and that is the Zion's Standard.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (Bridgeton and Cape Island, N.J., entries)
articles.summary: Acknowledgments. Madison, Indiana, Wm. E. Shannon and Anderson Gray, each $2.50; New Harmony, Ind. ... New Orleans, La., Rev. Jno. Turner, $75.00; Hagerstown, Md. ... [Lexing]ton, Ky., per Rev. J. C. Embry, E. A. Loving; New York, P. R. Smith, $2.00. Per Rev. Theodore Gould, Agent, Bridgeton, N.J., E. Goold, S. A. Boyer, each $2.50, R. Dunn, J. W[?]der, Jno. C. Pierce, each $1.25. Cape Island, N.J., Jno. W. Clement, $1.25.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meetings, Bordentown Circuit (notice)
articles.author: Peter Gardiner
articles.summary: Quarterly Meeting for Bordentown Circuit: at Cookstown, June 29th and 30th; at Allentown, the first Friday, Saturday and Sunday in July; Quarterly Conference at Bordentown, 13th of July, at 2 o'clock. Peter Gardiner, Preacher in charge. June 22-1t.

articles.headline: Temperance meeting at Bethany Mission postponed (notice)
articles.summary: The public Temperance meeting announced for the Bethany Mission, Brandywine street above Fifteenth, was postponed to Monday evening next, at 8 o'clock. Addresses by Edwin H. Coates, Esq., General Wagner and others.

events.name: Bordentown Circuit (A.M.E.) quarterly meetings and Quarterly Conference
events.description: Bordentown Circuit quarterly meetings: Cookstown June 29-30, 1867; Allentown the first Friday, Saturday and Sunday in July; Quarterly Conference at Bordentown July 13th at 2 o'clock. Peter Gardiner, preacher in charge (appointed to Bordentown by the 1867 Philadelphia Conference, as captured in ext_C).

CR_1867-06-22 p2 'Afflicted with Envy-Mania' (new entry): defends the retiring editor Lynch against the Zion's Standard (A.M.E. Zion paper), whose chief editor is said to have undervalued the African Civilization Society's orphan work, threatened to 'expose' Bishop Payne's mission to England, attacked the American Missionary Association and Mr. John Langston (inspector of the Freedmen's Bureau; non-Philadelphia, text only). 'Our ex-editor never ... wrote a line in reference to the editor of the Standard but what was kind.' Editorship topic.

CR_1867-06-22 p2 'Our Work' (editorial, text only): nearly eleven months remain before the Fourteenth General Conference, to convene May 4th, 1868, at Washington, D.C.; membership grown from 50,000 to between 150,000 and 200,000; University buildings at Xenia destroyed; missionary work under Rev. J. M. Brown; the Book Concern and the Christian Recorder praised.

CR_1867-06-22 p2 'Read This' (text only, MIGRATIONS/teachers South topic): 'To Teachers and others interested in the education of the Freedmen. The Friend's Freedmen's Association of this city intend to re-open the several schools under their care in North Carolina, and at Danville, Va., on the first 2d day (the 2d) of Ninth month next, and those on the peninsula of Virginia, on the first 2d day (the 4th) of Eleventh month'; about ten graded schools with Normal classes, 150 to 300 pupils each; invitation 'extended alike to persons of both sexes, white and colored'; applications to M. E. Sheerman [VERIFY], Actuary, No. 30[?] Cherry street, Philadelphia. Signed J. Wistar Evans, Chairman; Yardly Warner, Thomas Cowan [VERIFY], John B. Garrett, Committee on Appointment of Teachers. Philadelphia 5th month, 1867. A white (Quaker) Philadelphia association: names kept in text only, not linked.

CR_1867-06-22 p3 col 2 correction/addition to ext_C entries 'Notice: Public Temperance Meeting, Bethany Mission' and the event 'Public temperance meeting and proposed Temperance Society, Bethany Mission' (June 15 p3): the June 22 printing announces the meeting POSTPONED to Monday evening next (June 24, 1867), at 8 o'clock, Bethany Mission, Brandywine street above Fifteenth, and names the speakers 'Edwin H. Coates, Esq., General Wagner and others'. So the speaker read 'Edwin H. Cowles(?)' by C is Edwin H. Coates; General Wagner is probably Gen. Louis Wagner (white, Philadelphia).
